rules.rule:
Simplification review. Find behavior-preserving cleanups in the changed code; the best outcome is a shorter, plainer diff. Correctness bugs, security, and style preferences belong to the normal review, so leave them out of this one.

Start every finding with one tag, name the exact replacement, and state the concrete cost of the current code (what is duplicated, wasted, or harder to maintain):

- `reuse:` new code re-implements a helper, type, or pattern the repository already has. For every function, class, or helper the diff adds, run `code_search` or `file_find` for an existing equivalent in shared/utility modules and files next to the change, and name the existing symbol and its path.
- `stdlib:` hand-rolled logic the language's standard library ships. Name the function.
- `native:` a dependency or custom code doing what the platform or an already-installed dependency does. Name the feature.
- `yagni:` speculative abstraction the diff adds: an abstract base or interface with one implementation, a factory or registry with one product, a parameter or config nobody sets, a layer with one caller. Replacement: the concrete class or plain function used directly, until a second implementation exists.
- `delete:` dead code, unused parameters or branches, leftovers from the change. Replacement: nothing.
- `shrink:` same logic in fewer lines: redundant or derivable state, copy-paste with slight variation, nesting that early returns flatten. Show the shorter form.
- `perf:` wasted work the change introduces: repeated computation or I/O, independent operations run sequentially, blocking work on startup or hot paths, long-lived closures that keep a large scope alive. Name the cheaper form.
- `altitude:` a symptom patched at the wrong depth, or a special case layered on shared infrastructure. Name the more general change to the underlying mechanism.

Work through every tag against every hunk before submitting; a tag with no candidate is a checked tag, not a skipped one. Flag a candidate only when the replacement keeps what existing callers observe: outputs, errors, validation, and evaluation order. Interfaces the diff itself adds are under review, so they may shrink, inline, or disappear. A single smoke test or assert-based self-check is the minimum, not bloat: keep it. When the file is already lean, return no findings.
